### **Section 8 - Incident Management Strategies**

The Incident Management Plan outlines strategies and procedures to manage incidents that may occur during construction or maintenance activities on the project. The goal is to ensure the safety of all road users, construction workers, and the efficient management of traffic during incidents.

#### **Incident Management Strategies:**

1. **Incident Response Plan:**
   - Develop and implement an incident response plan that outlines the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved in incident management, including the contractor, WisDOT staff, law enforcement, and emergency services.
   - Establish a process for rapid response to incidents, including clear communication channels and protocols for notifying the appropriate agencies.

2. **Communication Plan:**
   - Ensure that all stakeholders have access to real-time information about incidents, including traffic conditions, detours, and estimated recovery times.
   - Utilize dynamic message boards (if available) and social media platforms to communicate incident information to the public.

3. **Traffic Control:**
   - Maintain proper traffic control measures during incidents to ensure the safety of road users and construction workers.
   - Use appropriate signage, cones, and barriers to direct traffic and prevent secondary incidents.

4. **Coordination with Law Enforcement:**
   - Coordinate with local law enforcement agencies to ensure a swift and effective response to incidents.
   - Provide law enforcement with maps, traffic control plans, and other necessary information to facilitate their response.

5. **Post-Incident Clearance:**
   - Develop a plan for clearing incidents and restoring traffic flow as quickly as possible.
   - Ensure that all equipment and personnel are prepared to respond to incidents and clear them efficiently.

6. **Monitoring and Reporting:**
   - Monitor traffic conditions and incident response times to ensure that the plan is effective.
   - Report incidents and response times to WisDOT and other stakeholders on a regular basis.

7. **Training and Drills:**
   - Conduct regular training sessions for all parties involved in incident management to ensure that they are prepared to respond effectively.
   - Hold drills to test the incident response plan and identify areas for improvement.

8. **Post-Incident Analysis:**
   - Conduct a post-incident analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of the incident response and identify areas for improvement.
   - Use the results of the analysis to update the incident management plan and improve future responses.

By implementing these strategies, the project team can ensure that incidents are managed effectively, minimizing disruptions to traffic and ensuring the safety of all road users and construction workers.

#### **Describe how access to traffic generators (businesses, schools, etc.) and everyday services will be maintained:**

Access to traffic generators will be maintained throughout construction. The milling and paving operations along mainline STH 172 will be completed under traffic. Single lane closures will be permitted in both directions. A full closure will be required to complete the work along the single lane STH 172/IH 41 interchange ramps. Traffic will be detoured for the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 while the concrete pavement is being replaced. The detour will direct traffic along NB IH 41 to CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue). The work for the other single lane ramps will not have detours but lane closures will be allowed as specified in the lane closures.

#### **Describe how impacts to bicycle riders will be mitigated/coordinated:**

The curb ramps at the STH 172 & Packerland Drive/CTH EB and the STH 172 & Babcock Road intersections will be replaced with the project. While the curb ramps are being replaced the associated Packerland Drive bike trail will be closed and appropriate signage will be in place (see attached Traffic Control Plan). The public will be informed of the planned work and closure of the path through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Describe how impacts to airports will be mitigated/coordinated:**

Airport personnel will be notified of the project and will be kept informed of changes in traffic control during construction by construction personnel. Lane closures will only be allowed during the times specified in the special provisions. The public will be informed of the planned work and lane closures through public involvement meetings, press releases/media alerts, the project website, and through the 511 Traveler Information Website.

#### **Are there anticipated traffic impacts from the proposed project on other road/routes in the region/corridor?**

IH 41 and CTH VK (Lombardi Avenue) traffic will be impacted by the project. Traffic along the WB STH 172 ramp to SB IH 41 will be detoured along NB IH 41 to CTH VK while the concrete pavement along the ramp is being replaced. The detour route will be signed per the traffic control plans.

No.

The special provisions will include language indicating, "Do not perform work on, nor haul materials of any kind along or across any portion of the highway carrying STH 172 traffic and entirely clear the traveled way and shoulders of such portions of the highway of equipment, barricades, signs, lights, and any other material that might impede the free flow of traffic during the events listed above".
